items_missed: No upfront agenda statement at the open — never framed 'I'll gather details, then walk you through pricing, takes 10-15 minutes' with a 'sound good?' confirmation; the only sequencing statement came after the hold, mid-call
Never asked 'How are you today?' — went straight from greeting into the move date
Never asked about packing services — customer was left to pack his own 20-25 boxes with no offer made
Never asked the moving-stressor question ('anything you're particularly worried about with this move?')
No 'no hidden fees' pitch — listed inclusions but never the explicit no credit card fee / no fuel surcharge / no assembly fee differentiator
No packing service pricing (hourly rate + materials) given
Clock explanation skipped 'the clock starts on-site when the contract opens' — jumped straight to the 2.5 hour minimum

Entire Save Your Ass prep speech missing — no prep-equals-shorter-move framing, no consolidation examples, no 'take a carload' tip, despite Phil volunteering 'I can bring them down' which was an open door

Variables not explained as time drivers — stairs (3-story origin + 2nd-floor walkup destination), walk distance, and traffic on a Houston-to-Fort Worth Friday were all gathered or relevant but never tied to the time range
No equivalents/visual reference (school bus, etc.) used, even though Phil said outright 'I'm real visual'

No booking attempt — never asked for the date after confirming availability; 'no deposit' only came out because Phil asked about it, and when he said he'd talk to his wife she closed with 'sure, I'll send everything'
Email handoff explained only as 'I'll send everything to your email' — no bolded key-details list at the top, no 'reply with any corrections' verification ask
Competitive pressure unacknowledged — Phil said in the first minute that another company had already contacted him and he was comparing prices; no value framing or urgency in response

Two-day vs one-day plan contradicted itself — she opened by asking permission to 'unload the next day,' then quoted a same-day load-drive-unload with the crew staying over afterward, without flagging the change
top_strength: The discovery was genuinely thorough and the resulting estimate was clean: she pinned both addresses, stories/stairs at both ends, item-by-item inventory, garage contents, appliances, fragile/valuable items, and walk distance at both the truck and the top of the stairs. The quote she built off it ($3,654-$3,858) reconciles exactly to 8.5-9.5 hours at $204 plus the $1,680 trip fee and $240 overnight fee.
coaching_note: Phil told her in the first minute he already had another mover and was 'still open comparing prices' — that is the whole call, and it went unanswered. She priced the job accurately, then let a warm, comparison-shopping lead walk with zero close: no ask for the Friday date after confirming availability, no Meet Your Mover, no On-Time Guarantee, no no-hidden-fees pitch, and no Save Your Ass prep speech that would have shown him how to cut his own bill. When a customer names a competitor, that is the cue to lead with differentiators and ask for the booking, not to promise an email and hang up.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and steady with good name use and a warm return from hold, but heavily transactional — filler acknowledgments ('Yup', 'Mm-hmm') carried most of her responses and she never acknowledged Phil's competing quote, his 'I'm real visual' comment, or any emotional cue.
